acceptedAnswer.text: The great-circle distance is divided by ground speed (aircraft speed plus wind along the route). Taxi, climb and approach time is then added to give a gate-to-gate figure.

mainEntity.name: Why is the flight home longer?

acceptedAnswer.text: In the middle latitudes the jet stream blows west to east, so eastbound flights get a tailwind and westbound flights a headwind. Transatlantic westbound trips are often about an hour longer.
The time from leaving the departure gate to arriving at the arrival gate. It is what airline timetables show.

mainEntity.name: How long does jet lag last?

acceptedAnswer.text: A common rule of thumb is about one day per time zone crossed when travelling east and about two-thirds of a day per zone travelling west. It varies a lot between people.

mainEntity.name: Why does the arrival day sometimes change?

acceptedAnswer.text: Crossing the date line or a long eastbound flight can land on a different calendar day in the destination time zone.
